decisions.title: AD-07 is still recorded OPEN, but Registry narrowing of max_amount, max_effects, target prefixes and target_match is merged
decisions.body: The frozen G0 decision register (docs/family-migration/g0/unresolved-decisions.md, AD-07) asks whether the Registry may ever carry these four fields, given Amendment 3 records them as caller-owned residuals, and lists it OPEN. Registry PRs #54 (r08-v3, merge ba98dd26) and #56 (r08-v4, merge b7e6a173) and Runtime PRs #151, #152 and #153 (merge f7a55e2a) implement exactly that narrowing, and the M2 record treats it as authorized. This audit found no later repository record that closes AD-07, so the register and the merged code disagree. It is a governance-record inconsistency, not a safety defect: the Runtime narrowing adapter was read and enforces subset-of-caller sets and ceilings no higher than the caller's.
decisions.recommendation: The Architect records an explicit disposition for AD-07 (ratify the merged M2/M3 narrowing, or direct a revert) so the register matches the code.

decisions.title: Counting rule: represented in the Registry is not governed
decisions.body: G0 labelled RG-A-007, RG-A-008 (and, in the audit's view, RG-C-021) ALREADY-GOVERNED. The Registry composes the F4 status/approval scalars and the F5 per-class map (registry_successor/v2_age_bounds.py), but the Control Plane imports no Registry code and enforces only host-supplied values; policy_binding.py enforces a host-copied age_ceilings. Three facts are therefore kept separate throughout this audit: represented in the Registry, integrated at an enforcement boundary, independently accepted. Only rules with the first two are REGISTRY-GOVERNED.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt the three-layer definition for backlog and PASS accounting; carry the F4/F5 age rules as eligible with the Registry half represented until the Control Plane consumer (waves M11/M12) is merged.

decisions.title: RG-C-018 (freshness nonce toggle) is not Registry-enforceable (superseded finding)
decisions.body: FreshnessProfile.nonce (default True) is host-settable and a forcing-True overlay would be monotone, but the resolver silently falls back to a plain read when it lacks nonce support (bounded.py:2208-2223), so a Registry cannot enforce it. Pass 1 first kept it ELIGIBLE (marginal); cross-check J2 and pass-2 Worker E reclassified it PROVIDER-OR-HOST-OWNED, which is the final disposition.
decisions.recommendation: None needed; recorded so the earlier ELIGIBLE reading is not relied on.

decisions.title: Two ocs-registry-record/0 formats exist
decisions.body: Repository-coverage worker I2 found the hub's tools/registry_records.py (lines 18-31) defines a second ocs-registry-record/0 format beside the Registry's r08-v2 record. Which one is the migration target, and whether the hub vocabulary must be reconciled with the Registry successor contracts, is not decidable from source.
decisions.recommendation: Architect names the authoritative record format; until then the rule NEW:hub-registry-record-profile-vocabulary stays UNRESOLVED.

decisions.title: Redaction defaults: floor or presentation choice?
decisions.body: The audit rates the Control Plane, Action Manifest and Replay Bundle redaction defaults CALLER-OR-ISSUER-OWNED (caller-overridable presentation defaults; no redaction floor exists in code), which removes the G0 eligible group RG-F11. A Registry 'minimum redaction' would be a new confidentiality control, not the migration of an existing one.
decisions.recommendation: If a minimum-redaction floor is wanted, treat it as a new privacy-owned feature (plan wave M10) with its own decision, not as a rule migration.

decisions.title: How a Registry-narrowed Control Plane class value enters approval_commitment
decisions.body: The whole ActionClass is hashed into approval_commitment (runtime_authority.py:236-247). Narrowing a per-class age, unreadable posture or revocation-assurance flag through a Registry record changes a committed value, so the commitment coupling must be defined before RG-C-008/C-009/C-010 (and the merged F5 class age rule) can be implemented.
decisions.recommendation: Decide the coupling in the M12 design before any F5 Control Plane consumer is authorized.
